# API reference

[Documentation](../index.md) · [Usage guide](../guide.md) · [Execution contracts](../library_contracts.md)

This reference describes the current source tree. Import public entry points from `warpack`.
It follows Warp's `Args`/`Returns` docstring convention; signatures, parameter descriptions
and output attributes below are generated from the library source. The released v0.2.0
wheel predates some current-main options; use documentation from your checkout/tag.

Constructors allocate persistent workspace; they do not return an eigensystem.
`solve()` returns the solver instance and writes device outputs. `capture()` returns a
CUDA graph which must be launched. Eigenvectors and singular vectors are **rows**.
See the [result and residual contracts](../guide.md#results-and-acceptance) before
interpreting convergence; the Hermitian, buckling and SVD wrappers have different fields.

Invalid parameter metadata is reported by Python exceptions during setup or dispatch.
Numerical failures may instead set device status/count fields: inspect the output
contract after execution. Construction and graph capture may allocate or synchronize;
device replay and explicit host result inspection are separate operations.

Only the entry points and methods listed here form this documented frontend.
Other exposed implementation stages and names beginning with `_` are internal.
In particular, `_working_matrix` and `_storage` are internal adapter plumbing,
retained in signatures for accuracy; callers should not supply them.

## [Symmetric and generalized eigensolvers](symmetric.md)

- [`BlockLOBPCG`](symmetric.md#blocklobpcg): Smallest algebraic eigenpairs of symmetric K x = lambda M x.

- [`KrylovSchur`](symmetric.md#krylovschur): Thick-restarted symmetric Krylov / Rayleigh–Ritz iteration.

- [`GeneralizedKrylovSchur`](symmetric.md#generalizedkrylovschur): Real symmetric A x = lambda M x, with SPD M, using mass-orthogonal Krylov.

- [`SymmetricEigensolver`](symmetric.md#symmetriceigensolver): FP64 orthogonal iteration with CholeskyQR2 and Rayleigh–Ritz.

- [`GeneralizedEigensolver`](symmetric.md#generalizedeigensolver): Solve A x = lambda B x for symmetric A and SPD B.

- [`BucklingEigensolver`](symmetric.md#bucklingeigensolver): A x = lambda B x, A SPD and B symmetric (possibly indefinite).

- [`CayleyEigensolver`](symmetric.md#cayleyeigensolver): A x = lambda B x, B SPD, ranked by |(lambda+sigma)/(lambda-sigma)|.

## [Complex and nonsymmetric eigensolvers](complex.md)

- [`HermitianEigensolver`](complex.md#hermitianeigensolver): Complex Hermitian eigenpairs through realified restarted Krylov iteration.

- [`GeneralEigensolver`](complex.md#generaleigensolver): Complex nonsymmetric eigenpairs with LM/SM/LR/SR/LI/SI selection.

- [`ShiftInvertEigensolver`](complex.md#shiftinverteigensolver): Eigenpairs nearest a real or complex sigma; original-problem residuals.

- [`GeneralizedShiftInvertEigensolver`](complex.md#generalizedshiftinverteigensolver): Finite right eigenpairs of `A x = lambda B x` nearest `sigma`.

## [Singular value decomposition](svd.md)

- [`PartialSVD`](svd.md#partialsvd): Largest k singular triplets of rectangular real FP64 CSR.

- [`NormalSVD`](svd.md#normalsvd): Largest resolved nonzero triplets of compact scalar FP64 CSR matrices.

## [Operators, sparse inverses and preconditioners](operators.md)

- [`SparseOperator`](operators.md#sparseoperator): FP64 scalar CSR or 3x3 BSR operator on row-major vector blocks.

- [`BatchedSparseOperator`](operators.md#batchedsparseoperator): FP64 CSR/3×3 BSR products sharing reads across adjacent RHS rows.

- [`HermitianCSR`](operators.md#hermitiancsr): Device complex CSR; values use wp.vec2d(real, imaginary).

- [`ComplexCSR`](operators.md#complexcsr): Complex CSR for a general square matrix, without a symmetry assumption.

- [`CuDSSInverse`](operators.md#cudssinverse): Factorization is setup work; apply() is graph capturable.

- [`CGInverse`](operators.md#cginverse): Pure-Warp SPD inverse with optional upstream Warp preconditioning.

- [`GMRESInverse`](operators.md#gmresinverse): Apply a real FP64 sparse inverse using unmodified upstream Warp GMRES.

- [`BatchedCGPreconditioner`](operators.md#batchedcgpreconditioner): Preallocated upstream batched CG with independent per-RHS tolerances.

- [`ComplexShiftInverse`](operators.md#complexshiftinverse): Apply (A-sigma I)^-1 using cuDSS or pure-Warp GMRES.

## [Constraints and subspace projection](constraints.md)

- [`ConstrainedKrylovSchur`](constraints.md#constrainedkrylovschur): H W + C.T mu = M W lambda, C W = 0, W.T M W = I.

- [`saddle_point_matrix`](constraints.md#saddle_point_matrix): Assemble [[H-shift*M, C.T], [C, 0]] using Warp sparse kernels.

- [`independent_constraints`](constraints.md#independent_constraints): Pure-Warp pivoted, twice-reorthogonalized row QR for small dense constraint spaces.

- [`OrthogonalComplementOperator`](constraints.md#orthogonalcomplementoperator): Apply `P operator P`, where `P = I - basis.T @ basis`.

- [`MassOrthogonalComplementInverse`](constraints.md#massorthogonalcomplementinverse): Apply `P inverse P.T` with `P = I - Q Q.T M` entirely on device.

## [Residuals, nullspaces and completeness](diagnostics.md)

- [`EigenpairEvaluation`](diagnostics.md#eigenpairevaluation): Evaluate fresh real standard-problem residuals for unit-norm vectors.

- [`NumericalNullspaceDiagnostics`](diagnostics.md#numericalnullspacediagnostics): Evaluate a fixed-capacity Ritz space of a real symmetric PSD pencil.

- [`LowestModeCertificate`](diagnostics.md#lowestmodecertificate): Numerical coverage of *all* eigenpairs below a supplied spectral gap.

- [`InertiaResult`](diagnostics.md#inertiaresult): Numerical inertia snapshot; `status == "available"` excludes suspect factors.
